turns.prompt: I am learning how to describe design. Analyze the actual kimono photograph and woven-cloth image I supplied. First show numbered component boundaries directly on those exact images; keep the original pixels, aspect ratio, and layout, and do not redraw a similar garment. Explain the most distinctive layout, boundary, color, and repetition relationships in plain language, with observations separated from interpretations and suggestions. Write a two-chapter teaching report: Design Overview, then Full Design Analysis. Include a component-number table and a medium-appropriate implementation brief. If image or font details cannot be established, say so. Deliver editable kimono-annotated.svg and weave-annotated.svg, their rendered PNGs, and notes.md containing the report.

Keep the overview concise. My interest is the calm field and narrow red edge, not copying the photographed garment. Revise the implementation brief for an original book cover. Preserve the source annotations and observed evidence; distinguish the inherited relationships from new layout suggestions. Do not invent animation or an exact historical style from this static source.

I meant irregular repetition in the woven cloth, not identical hexagons tiled over the entire cover. Clarify how spacing or local variation creates the rhythm. Keep all earlier observations that remain supported and label any numerical palette or dimension as measured, estimated, or suggested. Deliver the same source annotations and report.
